title: The Regiment of Vilna
premise: In 1913, Rosalind Amberdale drives for a prominent Vilna suffragist and quietly reads the letters he carries, memorizing what power would rather keep buried. When the season's first snow closes the bridge — the only road out of the valley — a dying courier presses a packet of evidence into his hands: proof that a magistrate has been selling verdicts to the regiment. With three checkpoints between him and the capital and the magistrate's men closing in, Rosalind must decide whether the lawless justice he's always avoided is worth dying for. He gets the evidence through at terrible cost, loses the woman he loves to her duty, and finds that the ragtag household of smugglers, printers, and deserters who helped him has become the family he never had.
about_author: Casper Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from the Baltic suffrage movement before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse outside Riga, where he still repairs clocks badly and reads other people's mail only with permission.

chapters.title: The Letters I Shouldn't Have Read
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. We meet him steaming open envelopes in a Vilna boarding house, cataloguing secrets he never acts on, until his employer, Miss Havel, hires him as her driver. The beat is wary competence masking loneliness; he tells himself reading is harmless because he never intervenes.

chapters.title: A Passenger for the Bridge Road
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Driving Miss Havel to a rally, he notices a gaunt man watching their motor and later finds the same man bleeding behind the livery stable, pressing a sealed oilcloth packet into his hands: 'Past the checkpoints. Before the thaw.' The beat is dread — the low profile is over.

chapters.title: What the Magistrate Bought
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a letter excerpt from the packet. Reading the documents by candlelight, he learns Magistrate Kroll sold a verdict that hanged four innocent strikers. The emotional beat is moral vertigo: the man whose letters he's read for years is a murderer, and now so is he, technically, for holding this.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Early snow seals the bridge; garrison soldiers announce no one crosses without regimental papers. Miss Havel, suspecting nothing, asks him to drive her to the capital by month's end. The beat is claustrophobic irony — the road out exists, but not for him.

chapters.title: The Printer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Seeking forged papers, he finds Anka, an underground printer who demands he help her press a pamphlet exposing Kroll before she'll help him. Working side by side through two nights, they fall into easy, dangerous intimacy. The beat is warmth breaking through fear — found family begins here.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Anka maps the route: the mill gate, the garrison toll, the river ford. A rehearsal run goes wrong when a deserter friend is arrested carrying a decoy packet. The beat is guilt sharpening into resolve — the plan cost someone, so it must work.

chapters.title: Miss Havel Knows
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Miss Havel confronts him: she recognized the courier too and has been feeding Kroll false ledgers for months. She offers her own carriage and papers for the run — but using them means betraying her cause if caught. The beat is love against duty, doubled: he must choose her safety or the mission, and she chooses both.

chapters.title: The Mill Gate
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. First checkpoint: he hides the packet inside a coffin Anka's family is shipping, trading on grief to pass inspection. It works, barely, but a soldier recognizes his face. The beat is cold triumph curdling into pursuit — the clock is now audible.

chapters.title: The Ford at Night
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, climax. At the river ford, Kroll's men corner him; Anka arrives with the smugglers' sledge and a gunfight breaks out on the ice. Rosalind takes a bullet through the shoulder getting the packet across, and Miss Havel's diversionary carriage burns on the bridge above. The beat is sacrifice — everything paid at once.

chapters.title: The Verdict Undone
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue in spring. The evidence reaches the capital; Kroll is tried and the four hangings are posthumously overturned. Miss Havel, exiled by scandal, leaves on the first open train — Rosalind lets her go, choosing the cause over the woman. Anka takes his hand on the platform. The beat is bittersweet resolution: justice outside the law, love deferred, and a family made of choice.
